text:
alex: FYI we're seeing a cluster-wide OOB flurry after a PSU group failed in rack r11. Some nodes dropped to secondary serial path and a subset booted into firmware defaults (UEFI toggled to 'restore on AC loss'). provisioning jobs are stuck. anyone available?

oncall-bot: [ALERT] oob-flap detected: rack=r11, affected_nodes=~10%. Incident INC-3121 opened automatically.

devops: grabbing logs now. sample from r11-n05:
```
[2025-06-12T03:14:21Z] oob-proxy: link-change primary->secondary
[2025-06-12T03:14:22Z] hw: psu-group failover
[2025-06-12T03:14:23Z] bios: policy: restore-on-acloss=1; secure_defaults_applied
```

maria: attached to serial of r11-n12 — during the failover the firmware presented the setup screen, Secure Boot state = enabled, and NIC PXE blob mismatch prevented the kernel from loading. That explains the provisioning timeouts.

sanjay: any scheduled BIOS/firmware pushes last night? vendor had a BMC micro patch to a canary set but no fleet BIOS job. The patch notes mention a "restore-on-power-loss" flag. if PSU flapped, BIOS could have reverted settings.

ciara: we didn't do a scheduled BIOS roll but there was a limited BMC rollout to 10% of racks. recommendation: don't mass-rollback. we'll throttle fixes and pull affected nodes out of the scheduler immediately.

alex: runbook check: `oob-inventory --rack r11 --status` => 48 nodes total: 8 in secure-defaults, 30 in expected state, 10 unreachable over OOB. marking unreachable as oob-unreachable and removing from provisioning pool.

leo: quick remediation is an IPMI toggle but it's risky across many BMCs. ipmitool example (use with rate-limit):
```
ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P **** raw 0x3a 0x10 0x00
```
This flips the secure flag on some vendors. We'll run concurrency=2 to avoid thrashing the serial mux.

devops: note on capacity: losing ~10% of GPU capacity in r11 pushes autoscaler to spin more hosts elsewhere; that affects costs and might push Dedicated customers into burst if we don't pre-empt.

maria: proposed plan: 1) tag affected nodes and move to maintenance 2) run throttled toggle job (P=2) to restore expected BIOS flags 3) validate provisioning logs and driver binds before returning to pool. No fleet-wide ops.

ciara: starting remediation script in throttled loop:
```
cat r11-affected.txt | xargs -n1 -P2 -I{} ./tools/bmc_restore_defaults_off.sh {}
```
Job queued id=3347.

oncall-bot: deploy-bot: remediation job 3347 started by ciara. progress: 0/8 nodes.

maria: post-toggle checks:
- `dmidecode -s bios-version` and `dmidecode -t bios | grep -i secure`
- `sudo journalctl -u provisioning-agent -n 200`
- monitor `oob-proxy` for repeated bridge flaps

leo: r11-n23 failed IPMI attempts, returns "BMC locked"; opened hardware escalation HW-789 with vendor for serial unlock.

sanjay: while vendor handles r11-n23, spin-up fallback capacity in eu-west-2 for critical tenants and alert support about potential Dedicated impact.

ciara: after throttled runs, 7/8 targeted nodes report expected BIOS state and rejoined provisioning; one node still vendor-locked. GPU drivers bound and health checks passed on recovered nodes.

devops: :thumbsup: followups: add PSU health preflight to BIOS/BMC rollout runbook, add 'last-power-state' check before applying defaults, and add a monitoring alert for serial-mux swapback events.

alex: added retro action items and set a temporary scheduling exclusion for rack=r11: `fleet-route set --exclude rack=r11` for 30m to avoid immediate rescheduling.

oncall-bot: INC-3121 status -> mitigated. tags: oob, psu-failover, uefi-defaults, rack-r11

support: messaging note sent to Dedicated customers likely affected; recommended compensation/burst options queued for sales ops.

maria: closing note: vendor firmware should not auto-apply secure defaults on AC transitions unless customer opt-in. I'll document and file a request with firmware owners.

leo: thanks team. capturing exact timestamps for postmortem.

sanjay: good job, we'll draft timeline and RCA for infra-retro."
